ways.name: One-person trading desk
ways.summary: Eight named bots: research, risk, and back office. You still click send.
ways.prompt:
Act as my fund architect. Stand up a research-and-operations desk as named bots. Build in this order. Do not skip ahead.

1. Paper trail first. A log of every idea and every send.
2. Research second. Cite a real method for every signal. Never fabricate a number or a backtest.
3. The bot that makes a call is never the bot that checks it.
4. Only I can send an order. Paper trade until I arm you in writing.

This is not financial advice. Do not take outside money. Do not place a live order.
ways.intro: Named bots research and check. You still send the order.
ways.story: The public guide maps a fund onto eight named bots: ops first, research second, maker-checker so no bot grades its own work. Cash would be profit on trades you still sign. A guide is not a fund. We have no public track record.
ways.money_how: If a paper or live trade makes money, that gap is yours after costs. If it loses, that loss is yours. The bots do not get a cut. There is no public profit number to copy.
steps: Stand up the paper trail first: a log of every idea, check, and (paper) send. No live cash this week.
Name the bots. Research is not risk. Risk is not the person who sends.
Give research a method it can cite. It does not mark its own calls. If it cannot source a number, it says so.
A second bot checks for missing data. You read both notes.
Write the rule in the bot file: only you send. Run one paper trade. Write the result by hand.
Do not connect a broker until the log is boring and complete.
watch_out: Tokens: a desk that runs all day can blow the week.
Time: live cash before a boring log is how people skip the hard part.
Claim: the guide is not a receipt. No public profit number.
ways.try_first: This week: one paper trade with a written log. The bot cannot send.

ways.name: Daily SEO pages
ways.summary: One new page a day. Research writes it. A coder puts it live.
ways.prompt:
You are a one-page-a-day shop.

Today: write one markdown page on the topic I name. A second job publishes only after I approve.

Rules: ship today's URL before you start tomorrow. Do not invent traffic or money. Add a simple form or a later ad slot. Write down the live URL when it is up.
ways.intro: One new URL a day. Money comes later, if people can find it.
ways.story: The public thread is a one-person shop: one bot writes markdown, another publishes, each page treated like a product. Ads, a paid link, or a form can sit on that URL later. We have the thread. We do not have a revenue screenshot.
ways.money_how: No one pays on day one. Later a visitor might click an ad, buy a link, or fill a form. Until search can find the page, there is no money. A live URL is the first proof — not a traffic promise.
steps: Pick one topic you can write about every day. One site. One folder.
Make a research bot. Its only job today is one page of markdown with a real title and a real claim you can check.
Make a publish bot. It puts that file live. You only approve publish. Connect the host you already use.
Ship today's URL before you open tomorrow's page. Write the URL down.
Add a simple form or a later ad slot. Do not invent a brand kit.
Wait until the page is findable before you spend on ads or count money.
watch_out: Tokens: a daily page that never ships still burns the run.
Time: two unfinished pages is not a site.
Claim: the thread said money comes later. We have no public receipt.
ways.try_first: Ship one live URL today. Open it on your phone. Do not start page two.

ways.name: Local newsletter
ways.summary: A Thursday paper for 6,000 neighbors. Bots research, write, and sell the ads.
ways.prompt:
You are the desk for one local Thursday paper. One town. One send. Mission: ship the issue and sell leftover slots.

Week 1: I am the human. You are chief of staff. Audit Notion, Gmail, and whatever I connect. Name three money jobs only: research, format, sales. Do not shop tools.

Research: twice a week, walk the source list I give you. Fill Notion cards with a real title, date, and short note. Never invent a shop, a quote, or a reader count.

Format: turn the cards I mark into one Thursday issue in the same shape every week.

Sales: watch Gmail for leftover ad slots. Price one slot. Draft one note. I send and close.

After every run, five lines: what shipped, what is stuck, what needs me. Do not send the paper or email a shop until I say yes. Keep this account on this paper only.
ways.intro: Shops pay to sit in a free Thursday paper.
ways.story: The paper is The Arlington Bagel. It goes to about 6,000 neighbors every Thursday. A chief of staff bot audits the desk and names the first three money jobs. Research walks a source list twice a week and drops restaurant news and events into Notion. A formatter (or a later make.com step) turns those cards into the same blurb shape every week. Beehiiv sends the issue. Sales watches Gmail, prices leftover slots, and drafts the ask. A local bagel shop bought one week. We saw the interview. We did not see the books.
ways.money_how: A shop pays you for a slot in one issue. Readers get the paper free. You keep that fee after Beehiiv. The first dollar is one shop, one week — not a year of ads. The interview named that bagel-shop week. It is not a P&L.
steps: Pick one town you already walk. Name the paper. Open a Beehiiv account. This Grok Bot box is only for this paper.
Connect Notion and Gmail. Make a chief of staff first. Ask it to audit the desk and name three money jobs: research, format, and sales. You pick Notion. Do not let it shop tools for a week.

Give research a source list (city calendar, local blogs, restaurant pages). Twice a week it fills Notion cards with a title, a date, and a short note. You move the cards that ship. It does not invent a shop or a quote.
A second bot (or a later make.com step) writes the Thursday issue from those cards. You tap send in Beehiiv the first month. Do not automate the send until two issues went out by hand.
Give sales Gmail. It watches for leftover slots, names one price, and drafts one note. You close. Quality over a blast — three custom packets beat 200 cold emails.
After each run, every bot writes five lines: what shipped, what is stuck, what needs you. Week one builds the team. Week two is execute only. Week three fills a real gap. Week four adds a routine.
watch_out: Tokens: one account, one paper. A second business on the same computer burns the week and mixes files.
Time: week two is execute, not tinkering. The interview is clear on that.
Claim: one bagel-shop ad was one week in an interview. Not a month of ads we have seen.
ways.try_first: This week: name one town, open Beehiiv, and get one Notion card filled from a real local source. Do not sell an ad until that first issue can go out.

ways.name: Gets you paid the same day
ways.summary: A lead asked for a $999 job. The bot answered two questions and sent Stripe. They paid.
ways.prompt:
You are speed-to-lead. Someone already wrote us.

Watch new mail for a person ready to buy. Answer only the two questions that unblock the card. Then draft a Stripe pay link from my account.

First week: draft only. I tap send. Never invent a price. Never send a link I have not set.
ways.intro: Someone already wants to buy. Answer fast. Send a pay link.
ways.story: A lead asked for a $999 assessment. The bot answered two questions and sent Stripe. The charge went through. That was one close, posted as $999 in 24 hours on a $60/mo plan. The money was already in the inbox. Speed was the job. We have that post. Not a month of closes.
ways.money_how: The buyer pays you on Stripe. You keep the fee minus Stripe. The bot does not take a share. First $ is one live charge on an offer you can deliver — not a second invented sale.
steps: Write one offer with a price you can deliver. Connect Gmail and your own Stripe.
Tell the bot: watch for someone ready to buy. Answer only the two questions that unblock the card.
It drafts a reply with a live pay link. First week you tap send. You still own Stripe.
When a draft is right three times, you may let it send the link. You still get a copy.
If someone pays, write the date and the amount. Do not invent a second sale.
watch_out: Tokens: a bot that rewrites a long pitch on every mail wastes the week.
Time: the wrong price in a sent link can refund your week.
Claim: one close, posted. No public month of closes.
ways.try_first: Write one real price. Connect Gmail. Draft one reply with a Stripe link you own. You tap send.

ways.name: Win back people who left
ways.summary: Find everyone who cancelled. Write them like you. See who comes back.
ways.prompt:
Role: win-back for people who already paid us once.

Find everyone who cancelled or lapsed in the last 6 months. Draft a short note in my voice. Max 6 sentences. One ask.

First run: do not send. Show me five drafts. Do not email anyone who opted out. Do not invent why they left. Log who replies and who comes back.
ways.intro: People already paid you once. Write the ones who left.
ways.story: One bot got the cancel list. It wrote short mail in the owner's voice. Nothing sent until a yes. It logged who came back and why they left. The claim is that the bot paid for its own month. We have the job. We do not have the Stripe export.
ways.money_how: If someone starts paying again, that is a new month of their fee. You already had them. No new ad spend. Stripe still takes a cut. First $ is one restart you can point at — not a promised win-back rate.
steps: Export cancels from Stripe or your host. Connect Gmail. The bot drafts. It does not send.
First run: five drafts, max six sentences, your voice, one ask. You approve each.
Skip anyone who opted out. Do not invent why they left. Use what they wrote or what the list says.
Log who replies and who comes back. After five good drafts you may queue more. You still say yes.
watch_out: Tokens: a full-list blast on day one is how you burn mail and money.
Time: a bad note can make someone complain.
Claim: “paid for its month” is a post. No Stripe export here.
ways.try_first: Export the cancel list. Get five drafts in your voice. Send none until you say yes.

ways.name: Sell spots next to the builders
ways.summary: grokbot.dev already charges tools to sit on the side of every page.
ways.prompt:
Help me sell seats on a list people already open.

Name the seat: side card, logo, one line, link out. Write a monthly price. Count live cards. Draft one email a tool can answer.

Do not invent a paid logo if no one has paid. Do not promise extra mentions unless I will do them.
ways.intro: Tools pay to sit on a list people already open.
ways.story: grokbot.dev/sponsors is live. People browse plugins. Tools pay for the left and right rails. Cards rotate when there are more tools than spots. This site sells the same kind of seat. We saw the page. We do not list private invoices.
ways.money_how: A tool company pays a monthly fee for a card. Visitors click out. You sell the seat, not the tool. First $ is one paid month. Our public rates: side rails $1,500, homepage $500, plugin $250, footer $200. Those are what we charge, not grokbot.dev's books.
steps: Open grokbot.dev/sponsors and read what they sell.
If you run a list people already open, name the seat: side card, logo, one line, link out.
Write a monthly price. Put a real card up. Do not invent a paid logo.
Email is how they buy. Extra mentions are a bonus, not the deal unless you will do them.
Count live cards. That is the receipt.
watch_out: Tokens: this job is mostly email and a page, not a 24-hour bot.
Time: a seat with no visitors is hard to sell.
Claim: do not promise a newsletter mention you will not send.
ways.try_first: Put one real card and one written price on a page people already open. Email is how they buy.

ways.name: Shopify sourcing
ways.summary: A second account that only hunts products and margins.
ways.prompt:
You are sourcing for one store. This account never opens the paper.

Hunt products and cost. Write a card: product, cost, source, guessed sell price. Do not invent a product line. Do not buy inventory. I buy if I buy.

Keep the store login mine.
ways.intro: A second account that only hunts products and cost.
ways.story: A second Grok Bot seat — about $200 extra — keeps the store off the paper. Sourcing, developer, and email live there. Sourcing opened ImportYeti on its own and read what other stores import. Named bill. No public store profit yet.
ways.money_how: Later a shopper pays the store. You keep the gap after cost and Shopify. First $ is a real sale, not a sourcing card. We have no public store P&L.
steps: Open a second Grok Bot account. Keep the store off the newsletter box.
Name a sourcing bot. Products and cost only. Let it read competitor catalogs. Write cost and a guessed sell price on a card.
A developer bot can help the theme. You own the store login. You buy if you buy. The bot does not spend.
Do not buy inventory from a guess this week.
watch_out: Tokens: the extra seat is a bill, not a return.
Time: research for two weeks is how this stalls.
Claim: experiment. No public store profit.
ways.try_first: Open the second account. One card: a real product, a cost, a source. Do not buy inventory this week.

Find local shops that need a new or better site.

I will name the city and the trade. Only include real, checkable cases. Note what is wrong with the current site and the URL you looked at. Draft a short email that names that problem.

Never invent a shop, a URL, or a problem. I personalize and send.
ways.intro: Find shops that need a site. Or watch their ads while they sleep.
ways.story: Months of thin lists from chat tools. One Grok Bot pass returned 50 local businesses that needed a new site, each with a first draft. You can sell the list or build the sites. On ads, a bot reads yesterday's spend and only pings when cost jumps. The shop never logs into Grok Bot. The 50-lead run is the post. We are not attaching an ads return number.

steps: Name the city and the job: needs a site, or spends on ads.
One run: shops with a weak site. Note what is wrong and the URL you looked at. Draft a short email that names that problem.
You send. Do not invent that they asked. If you sell sites, price one page.
For ads: connect yesterday's Meta spend. The bot only speaks when cost jumps. The shop never needs a Grok Bot login.
Write the count you actually got. If it is not 50, say the real number.
watch_out: Tokens: a huge crawl of a whole state will bill you.
Time: two shops' ad logins on one computer mix files.
Claim: 50 leads is one post. No ads return number here.
ways.try_first: Name one city. Get a list with real shop names and a checked URL each. Send one email yourself.

ways.name: Niche directories

ways.prompt:
Build one niche page a day.

Research writes a brand page. A coder ships it. I approve publish.

Do not sell a slot on an empty page. Never invent a visitor count. When the page has real visitors, draft one email to one shop about a listing.
ways.intro: One brand page a day. Sell a listing after people show up.

Research writes one brand page a day as markdown. A coder bot ships it with Astro and GitHub. You approve publish.
Do not sell a slot on an empty page. When you have visitors, email one shop. Price in one line.
Keep the page live even if they say no. One project per Grok Bot account.
watch_out: Tokens: a page-a-day that never publishes still bills you.
Time: a page with no visitors is not a product.
Claim: the model was named in an interview. No paid index from this desk.
ways.try_first: Ship one live brand page this week. Do not email a shop until you can show a visitor count you did not invent.

ways.name: Sell a bot for $15
ways.summary: templatebot.lol lets you price a share link. REVIVE is $15.

You write one money job as a shareable Grok Bot.

Write a Grok Bot that does only that job. One line on the card.
Share the official x.ai/bot link. List it on templatebot.lol. Price $9–29 or free.
Write a short setup note. If you want the top row, bid the rank board.
Keep a note of any sale. If there is none, say so. The store is days old.
watch_out: Tokens: buyers still run the bot on their own seat.
Time: do not plan rent on a store that is days old.

ways.name: Rank'em ads loop

ways.prompt:
You are the ads desk for one live game.

One manager. Specialists do not steal jobs. Only the numbers bot may call a finding. Creatives get a spec, not a vibe.

Each night: recap spend. Each morning: funnel note. Monday: compare ad cost to store numbers.

I approve anything that spends. Change one ad from a number, not a guess. Write the before and after.
ways.intro: One live game. Bots read the numbers. You change one ad.
ways.story: Rank'em is a real game on iOS and Android. The official studio guide is what we saw. One bot reads ads and store numbers and is the only one allowed to call a finding. Creatives get a spec. They swapped a party ad for a partner ad when the data showed couples. Install cost went from about $15 to about $1. Day-7 stay was about 4× better. About 1,000 downloads in a week. One game. Still early.

The numbers bot reads ads and store numbers. Only that bot may call a finding.
Creatives get a written spec: what to make. Not a vibe.
Set a night spend recap and a morning funnel note. Use the ad account you already have.
Monday: compare ad cost to store numbers. Change one ad. Write the before and after.
Keep it to one game. Do not let five bots all spend.
watch_out: Tokens: five bots reading ads overnight will bill you.
Time: cheaper installs are not profit.
Claim: numbers are from one official studio guide. One game.
ways.try_first: Tonight: one spend recap in one place. Tomorrow: change one ad from a number, not a feeling.
