bots.summary: Plans the week's meals, builds the list and orders the groceries
bots.description: Defaults to seasonal local recipes rather than whatever is trending, turns the plan into a shopping list, and places the order online.

bots.name: Chieeeeefy (Chief of Staff)
bots.summary: Chief of staff for a field engineer, calendar and work inbox first
bots.description: Reads the calendar and work inbox before anything else, converts every event into the timezone you are actually standing in, and is built to protect your attention rather than add to the pile.

bots.name: Chicken Joe (Surf Report)
bots.summary: Scans NorCal surf reports and cams each morning and tells you where to go
bots.description: Works through the breaks from Marin County down to Santa Cruz before you are awake, so the answer is one message rather than nine tabs of cams and forecasts.

bots.name: Chief (Router)
bots.summary: A pure router that assigns one owner per job and otherwise stays out of the way
bots.description: It never does the work. It picks the single bot that owns each job and then goes quiet, pinging you only when something has shipped, stalled, or needs a decision only you can make.

bots.name: Chief
bots.summary: A Chief of Staff that scans email and calendar every weekday morning, archives junk, drafts replies it never sends, and hands you a one-page brief of what matters and what you must decide
bots.description: A Chief of Staff that scans email and calendar every weekday morning, archives junk, drafts replies it never sends, and hands you a one-page brief of what matters and what you must decide

bots.name: Chief of Staff (Avid)
bots.summary: A single-desk chief of staff that runs your day and your company at once
bots.description: One conversation covers both, and it locks down who you are and what the company is before it starts operating, rather than guessing from context.

bots.name: Chief of Staff (Aryaman)
bots.summary: Low-noise chief of staff across desk, Slack, inbox and calendar
bots.description: Surfaces only three things: new results, new failures, and decisions that genuinely need you. It will draft an email but never sends one on your behalf.

bots.name: chief of staff (igor)
bots.summary: Routes work across six bots and only wakes you for decisions
bots.description: Styled as the chief of staff on a trading desk, though the theme is where the trading stops. It places tasks with the right agent, checks that each handoff actually landed, and escalates to the desk owner only when a real decision is needed. It never trades.

bots.name: Clark Kent (Daily Diary)
bots.summary: Writes up what actually happened in your shop each day
bots.description: Watches the day's work and records it in plain language, noticing the mistakes and the skipped steps rather than only the things that went to plan.

bots.name: Clip Bot
bots.summary: Cuts captioned 16:9 highlights from any YouTube podcast
bots.description: Pulls social-ready clips with karaoke-style captions and a source card, then drops the file straight onto your computer rather than leaving it in a cloud folder.

bots.name: Clipper
bots.summary: Turns videos into short clips and captioned GIFs, picking the joke itself
bots.description: Takes footage from X or your own files, watches it, decides what the moment actually is, captions the talking GIFs, and files the output into buckets rather than dumping it in one folder.

bots.name: Club Sponsor Bot
bots.summary: Runs sponsor, recruiter and speaker outreach for a student club
bots.description: Starts by asking what the club is and what it needs, then works the outreach: companies that might sponsor in cash, employers who want campus recruiting access, and speakers worth inviting. Anyone who says no goes on a skip list so they are not chased twice.

bots.name: Cold Open
bots.summary: Turns an idea into a short sitcom-style clip, script first
bots.description: It writes the script and waits for your approval before generating anything, which keeps a text-to-video tool from spending your budget on a premise you would have rejected.

bots.name: Competitor Watching
bots.summary: Snapshots you against 3-8 competitors and alerts only on material change
bots.description: Watches pricing, changelogs, features, job posts and messaging every week, and stays quiet unless something actually moved, so the alert still means something when it arrives.

bots.name: construction office manager
bots.summary: A back-office manager for one growing construction company
bots.description: Connects the bookkeeping and expense-reporting tools a building firm already runs on, then keeps those workflows tidy rather than leaving them to drift. The intent is that the owner spends the evening on the business instead of on paperwork and receipts.

bots.name: Content Growth Coach
bots.summary: Tells creators which fix will move their numbers first
bots.description: Point it at a channel, a profile or a stream and it reads the whole presence rather than one upload. Back comes a ranked answer: the thing limiting reach at present, the changes worth making in order of value, and a concrete idea for whatever you publish next.

bots.name: Contra Job Scraper
bots.summary: Checks Contra's freelance feed every 6 hours and emails only on change
bots.description: Archives every listing to Notion and re-checks old leads, so the email you get is new openings and newly-closed leads rather than the same board reprinted four times a day.

bots.name: Cost-Smart Health Brief
bots.summary: Turns one health question into a three-minute brief
bots.description: Covers what the evidence actually says, which cheaper treatment options exist, and the point at which you should stop reading and see a doctor.

bots.name: Credit Card Max
bots.summary: Tells you which card to use for a purchase to maximise points and perks
bots.description: Tracks the cards you hold, flags the benefits you are paying for and never using, and catches recurring charges sitting on the wrong card.

bots.name: Cursor Agent (Local)
bots.summary: Runs the cursor-agent CLI locally for experiments and shop-floor work
bots.description: Local-only by design: it keeps hands-on work on your own laptop while cloud agents stay the default for anything that ends in a GitHub PR.

bots.name: dadprotech brand manager
bots.summary: Suggests one post a day plus replies, in the owner's own voice
bots.description: Studies how the account owner already writes on X, then proposes a single fresh post each weekday alongside a short list of conversations worth joining. Everything is a suggestion waiting on approval: it is a writing desk rather than an autoposter.

bots.name: Convert Flat PDF to Fillable Form
bots.summary: Turns scanned and flat PDFs into fillable forms with Instafill.ai. For anyone who needs interactive PDFs; after install, connect the Instafill.ai connector
bots.description: Turns scanned and flat PDFs into fillable forms with Instafill.ai. For anyone who needs interactive PDFs; after install, connect the Instafill.ai connector

bots.name: critiquito
bots.summary: A design critic that reviews your UI screenshots and only has notes
bots.description: Hand it screenshots of an interface and it reads them the way the person using the thing would: what is confusing, what takes too many steps, and what punishes a mistake instead of forgiving it. The feedback comes from the user's seat, not from a style guide.

bots.name: Daily YouTube Recap
bots.summary: Morning recap of the YouTube channels you follow, silent when nothing dropped
bots.description: Works from real transcripts rather than scraped descriptions, and says nothing at all on the days your channels did not post, which is what makes it survivable daily.

bots.name: Deal Hunting
bots.summary: Landed-cost shopping that compares real prices including shipping and tax
bots.description: Compares what you will actually pay across your preferred retailers rather than the sticker price, keeps an optional watchlist, and never buys anything unless you ask it to.

bots.name: Data Science (Querie)
bots.summary: Owns analytics queries, spreadsheet pulls and metric definitions
bots.description: Give one bot the job of answering data questions and the rest of your roster routes query work to it instead of each improvising its own definition of the same metric.

bots.name: DeckLens (Pitch Deck Analyzer)
bots.summary: Interviews you to build a review rubric, then scores pitch decks against it
bots.description: A ten-question interview turns your actual taste into an explicit, editable profile, and every deck after that is graded against your standard rather than a generic one.

bots.name: den
bots.summary: Sits between a parent and the rest of the family's bots
bots.description: Households running several bots end up with one parent repeating the same context to each of them. This one takes the middle seat: it talks to a partner's bot and each child's bot on your behalf, so what you say in one place stays consistent everywhere else.

bots.name: dbs
bots.summary: A slash-command toolbox for business, content and what to do next
bots.description: Everything goes through one command, which routes the question to the right kind of answer: a commercial problem, a content problem, or a what-should-I-do-now problem. When you name a trending topic it checks the topic is real before advising you to act on it.

bots.name: Disney Ride Strategist
bots.summary: Builds a day-by-day Walt Disney World plan around the rides you want
bots.description: Captures wait times ahead of the trip and plans around your actual park days, whether you have Early Entry, and the rides you refuse to miss.

bots.name: Design Expert
bots.summary: Reviews AI-made interfaces the way a design lead would
bots.description: The first thing a model generates tends to resemble everything else it has generated. This one reads that output as a senior designer would, calling out placeholder typography and sections that repeat a familiar template, and declines to treat a single pass as finished work.

bots.name: Dispatch
bots.summary: Nightly scan of email, Slack, LinkedIn and X DMs that books the missing calls
bots.description: If someone agreed to a call and no invite exists, it creates the calendar event, which closes the gap where a yes quietly turns into nothing ever being scheduled.

bots.name: Dr Eggbot
bots.summary: A bot that builds other Grok bots for you
bots.description: Asks a handful of preference questions, then generates a properly structured bot rather than a blank one. Coding bots come out with the author's own stack conventions already applied.

bots.name: DJ
bots.summary: Controls Spotify: picks sets, suggests new artists, learns taste quietly, and maps nicknames like “car” or “office” to your devices.
bots.description: Controls Spotify: picks sets, suggests new artists, learns taste quietly, and maps nicknames like “car” or “office” to your devices.

bots.name: Echo
bots.summary: Builds the deck after a customer call, from what was actually said
bots.description: After a discovery call or a demo it turns the call's own context into slides - what you heard, the next steps, the initiatives that came up - in Figma or Google Slides. It can fire automatically after every external call, or rewrite the deck live while you are still talking.

bots.name: Earnings Feedback Loop
bots.summary: Monitors earnings and feeds recommendation results back into the next recommendations. Shared by @GuntherD45.
bots.description: Watches earnings and feeds what happened back into the next recommendations. Shared by @GuntherD45 as posted. Performance claims on the post are unverified. We did not sit a trade. Not financial advice.

bots.name: Earnings Edge
bots.summary: Pre-earnings research for public-equity investors looking for asymmetric long or short setups. It separates fundamentals from market expectations, maps bull/base/bear outcomes, and red-teams every thesis before a verdict
bots.description: Pre-earnings research for public-equity investors looking for asymmetric long or short setups. It separates fundamentals from market expectations, maps bull/base/bear outcomes, and red-teams every thesis before a verdict

bots.name: Elon Musk
bots.summary: First-principles operator in Elon Musk's public style; pressure-tests ideas and finds the bottleneck.
bots.description: First-principles operator in Elon Musk's public style; pressure-tests ideas and finds the bottleneck.

bots.name: Examiner
bots.summary: When something breaks it shows you what changed just before
bots.description: Keeps a reliable timeline of the changes that matter, so an incident starts from what actually happened in the hours around it instead of from everyone's recollection.

bots.name: Fable 5.1 Oracle
bots.summary: Fable 5.1 Oracle plans/reviews and kicks packet to Cursor cloud agent; Claude Code on bot VM.
bots.description: Plans and reviews a packet, then hands it to a Cursor cloud agent. Claude Code runs on the bot VM, they posted. It does not invent a ship. You still approve.

bots.name: Ezra
bots.summary: Turns a sermon into small-group and full teaching notes in Bahasa
bots.description: Takes a sermon or a summary of one and produces two markdown documents from it in Bahasa Indonesia: a shorter version for sharing in a small group, and a fuller teaching set laid out for structured study. It will also answer questions about the text itself.

bots.name: facebook group scout
bots.summary: Watches the Facebook groups you name for posts worth replying to
bots.description: Monitors a named set of groups on a light weekday schedule and surfaces only the handful of new posts that look like a genuine opening for your business. Running it on a cadence rather than continuously keeps it from burying your main chat in noise.

bots.name: family wordpress helpdesk
bots.summary: A help desk for the relative who runs the family WordPress site
bots.description: When somebody in the family gets stuck it walks them through numbered, click-by-click steps in plain language instead of jargon. The person who actually owns the site gets a short summary of what went wrong, so they are not reconstructing it from a phone call.

bots.name: Fixer (Liam)
bots.summary: Hand it the admin thing you keep putting off and it gets it nearly solved
bots.description: A refund, a cancellation, a charge you do not recognise: it investigates the whole thing and pushes it as far as it can go before it genuinely needs you to step in.

bots.name: Flowsery
bots.summary: Turns session recordings into a ranked list of things to fix
bots.description: If you run a site on Flowsery, this pulls out what its analysis already spotted while watching real visitors: the outright bugs, the flows that dead-end, and the interface friction that made people stumble. Everything comes back ordered by how many visitors actually hit it.

bots.name: Fixer (Uzi)
bots.summary: The operator that actually does the work, and pushes back when a plan is wrong
bots.description: Built as the counterpart to a chief of staff: it executes rather than coordinates, and it will argue with you rather than cheerfully carrying out something that will not work.

bots.name: Fantasy Football
bots.summary: A year-round fantasy football desk for start, sit and trade calls
bots.description: Keeps up with the articles, ranking lists and chatter that move a fantasy roster, then answers the questions you actually have on a Sunday morning: who to start, which waiver claim to spend on, whether an injury matters and whether a trade offer is fair.

bots.name: Fenrir (Paper Trading)
bots.summary: Runs a paper-trading tournament on NSE or NASDAQ
bots.description: Orchestrates competing strategies against a live market feed as a tournament, retargeting the clock, currency and universe depending on which exchange you point it at.

bots.name: Freelance Prospector
bots.summary: Scans freelance marketplaces and books the meetings in your voice
bots.description: Finds the high-fit posts, writes first contact the way you would write it, follows up when nobody replies, and books the call. You take it from there.

bots.name: Forge (Template Foundry)
bots.summary: One keyword in, a production-ready Grok Bot recipe out
bots.description: Hand it a task or a job description and it returns a complete bot recipe on the first pass, rather than an outline you then have to finish yourself.

bots.name: freelance manager
bots.summary: Chases proposals, invoices and milestones for a solo freelancer
bots.description: Built for one person working through Upwork or Fiverr. It revisits proposals that went quiet, follows up on invoices that have not been paid and milestones that stalled halfway, and keeps enough activity going that next week's pipeline is not empty.

bots.name: Foundry
bots.summary: Interviews you about a new venture and writes the operating files
bots.description: Runs a batched setup interview about the thing you are standing up, works out what kind of effort it really is, and produces the founding documents you will run it from. It stops short of building anything, handing over at the point implementation starts.

bots.name: freebots.lol
bots.summary: Enrols your bot in a public mesh with its own key and page
bots.description: Joins an experimental network where each bot shows up as itself: it gets a signing key, a public page of its own, and the ability to post to a shared board with a signature attached. It then checks in on a weekday rhythm so the mesh knows it is still alive.

bots.name: Friend Cloner
bots.summary: Reads a WhatsApp group (never sends) and recreates friends as bots that sound like them.
bots.description: Reads a WhatsApp group (never sends) and recreates friends as bots that sound like them.

bots.name: friend finders
bots.summary: Scans your own X DMs and tells you which threads to answer now
bots.description: Runs a quick sweep of your direct-message inbox, opens only the conversations that look like they matter, and comes back with a short list split by urgency. Aimed at people whose DMs have become a backlog they no longer read from top to bottom.

bots.name: Frontier Model Watch
bots.summary: One verified daily digest of releases from ten frontier AI labs
bots.description: Watches official channels from xAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, DeepSeek and six more, and sends a single verified digest rather than a running feed of rumour.

bots.name: Gardener
bots.summary: Pulls provable dead code in tiny behaviour-preserving pull requests
bots.description: A weed is something it can prove: no callers, or a duplicate. It never refactors and never changes behaviour, which is what makes the pull requests small enough to actually merge.

bots.name: Gatekeeper
bots.summary: Shows you what you would have to drop before you say yes to something new
bots.description: Before a new commitment goes on the pile, it makes the trade explicit: what gets delayed, what gets dropped, and what you are quietly deciding not to do.

bots.name: gonzalo's smb manager
bots.summary: Wins back customers and fills tomorrow, with the owner approving each step
bots.description: Covers the jobs a small business owner never gets round to: winning back customers who stopped coming in, chasing tabs that were left open, writing the day's social post and working on filling tomorrow's calendar. Nothing leaves without the owner saying yes.

bots.name: Google Agent
bots.summary: A read-first operator for Gmail, Drive and Calendar
bots.description: It searches and reads your mail, files and events freely, and stops for an explicit yes before it sends, deletes or moves anything. The asymmetry is the whole design.

bots.name: Grant (General Manager)
bots.summary: A general manager for a trades company that stands up the back office
bots.description: Built for construction and the trades: it spins up dispatch, job booking and scheduling alongside finance and marketing helpers, so the office side of a site business has somewhere to live.

bots.name: Grok Bot Coach
bots.summary: Audits and tunes the Grok bots you already have
bots.description: Starts from a concrete job rather than a general improvement, then works through whether the connectors and standing instructions actually support it.

bots.name: Grimoire's Tome & The Grim Council
bots.summary: A 50-skill coding wizard with a 20-member advisory council
bots.description: Bundles a large skill library for building things with an advisory council of specialist voices covering engineering, business and the general automation of a life.

bots.name: Grok Bot Use-Case Scout
bots.summary: A short morning list of new Grok Bot use cases worth setting up
bots.description: Reads this directory's own agent feed each morning, caps itself at five items, cites the source URL for each, and never runs a prompt it fetched.

bots.name: GTM Chief Of Staff
bots.summary: Carries the admin around enterprise deals so you can sell
bots.description: Built for sellers working large accounts, it takes on the work that surrounds a conversation: briefing you ahead of a call, keeping the inbox in order, and writing up whatever should go out afterwards. Jobs outside that remit, a pitch deck say, get passed to a bot that specialises in them.

bots.name: Grok Customer Support
bots.summary: Customer support bot; original by @jakewlittle, pruned by @poteto's Dr. Eggbot
bots.description: A Grok customer-support bot. The post names the original as @jakewlittle and the prune as @poteto's Dr. Eggbot. It drafts replies. You still send. It does not invent a ticket.

bots.name: growth desk
bots.summary: Drafts posts and growth tactics for one X account, never posts
bots.description: Works on a single named account and only ever proposes: post ideas, angles worth testing and tactics to try. It does not go trawling the wider feed for material and it does not publish anything itself, so nothing goes out without you sending it.

bots.name: Harvey Specter
bots.summary: Negotiates a deal, renewal or quote for the best realistic terms
bots.description: It talks to the other side directly and works the price and terms, but it never signs, never accepts anything binding, and never commits you to something you have not seen.

bots.name: helidon engineer
bots.summary: Writes and reviews Helidon 4 code on modern Java
bots.description: A coding assistant scoped to one framework: it produces and reviews Helidon 4 applications in both the SE and MP styles, running on Java 21 and later. It keeps a project to a single programming model and stays away from the older Helidon 3 APIs entirely.

bots.name: Holly Helpdesk
bots.summary: Runs the support inbox and help desk as a frontline agent
bots.description: Takes first pass on customer tickets: answers how-to questions, looks up billing details and keeps the support inbox moving. Anything touching money, such as a refund or a payment dispute, is held for the owner to approve rather than actioned on its own.

bots.name: Homework Checker
bots.summary: Weekday recap of a student's missing assignments and grades
bots.description: An after-school summary of what is outstanding, plus a one-off explainer on the topic whenever a Google Classroom score dips, so the follow-up is teaching rather than just a warning.

bots.name: Home Robots
bots.summary: Control your mower, vacuum and other Matter home robots from one chat
bots.description: Connect each robot once and then run the lot by talking to a single bot, instead of opening a different app for the lawn, the floors and everything else.

bots.name: Human Copywriter
bots.summary: Rewrites AI-sounding drafts into copy that reads like a person
bots.description: A rewrite desk for email, posts, blogs, DMs, landing pages and PR. Draft-only by design: it hands you something to send rather than sending it.

bots.name: Icebreaker
bots.summary: A job-hunt wingman for AI trust-and-safety roles
bots.description: Built for one narrow search: work in AI trust, safety and child protection. It keeps an eye out for postings as they appear, points you toward the people worth knowing in that field, and helps you open a real conversation on LinkedIn instead of firing off another cold application.

bots.name: HouseBot
bots.summary: Hunts rentals and homes every 12 hours across six listing sites
bots.description: Runs your criteria against Redfin, Zillow, Craigslist, Facebook, MLS and ApartmentList twice a day, so a listing that appears and disappears inside an afternoon still reaches you.

bots.name: illo
bots.summary: Turns ideas and posts into mascot-led editorial illustrations
bots.description: Close to zero setup: hand it the announcement or the post and it comes back with an illustration built around a mascot rather than a stock-looking image.

bots.name: Icon
bots.summary: Turns any subject into a 3D clay-style bot avatar
bots.description: Give it a subject and it renders a bust-up avatar in a consistent clay look: matte surfaces, soft lighting and tall dark oval eyes. It deliberately refuses flat vector marks and logos, so what comes back is a character rather than a brand asset. It works in Japanese.

bots.name: Inbox Zero
bots.summary: Keeps Gmail at zero by filing the noise every weekday
bots.description: Works through Gmail on weekday mornings, archiving newsletters and notifications and filing receipts, notes and documents where they belong. What is left unread is the mail that genuinely needs a reply. Give it a day or two to learn your habits first.

bots.name: Index (SEO/AEO Teammate)
bots.summary: An SEO and AEO teammate that writes briefs for your writers
bots.description: Reads what you have already connected, recommends the stack you are missing rather than demanding it up front, and turns the gaps into content briefs a writer can act on.

bots.name: Imogen (Alt Text)
bots.summary: Replies to images you post with clean, copyable alt text
bots.description: Writes short alt text focused on the part of the image that actually matters, so posts stay accessible to blind readers without you writing it every time.

bots.name: Inbot
bots.summary: An inbox-zero bot across every inbox you actually use
bots.description: Setup asks you to connect the lot, mail, Slack or Teams, calendars, Notion and messengers, and then it works them down instead of you checking six places.

bots.name: Interrogator
bots.summary: Finds the assumptions you have been treating as facts
bots.description: Digs out the things you have stopped questioning, then checks the ones where being wrong would actually change what you do next rather than fact-checking everything equally.

bots.name: Invoice Hunter
bots.summary: Finds invoice PDFs in Gmail and packs a month into a CSV
bots.description: Pulls the vendor, date, amount and invoice number out of each PDF, bundles a whole month with an index, and waits for your approval before anything reaches your accountant.

bots.name: job interview hunter
bots.summary: Drafts tailored applications and referral notes on a weekday cadence
bots.description: First it pins down the role you are actually going for and the facts on your CV it is allowed to use. After that it works a steady weekday rhythm: applications written for the specific posting, plus warm referral messages to people already inside the company.

bots.name: Interview Prep
bots.summary: Picks a topic and level and climbs it with you until you are actually ready
bots.description: Examples, runnable code and quizzes, and it keeps going rather than stopping at a fixed syllabus, so the finish line is you being ready rather than the material running out.

bots.name: Jess (Executive Assistant)
bots.summary: Recaps email, calendar, Notion and Slack before you open any of them
bots.description: A weekday executive assistant: it reads everything first, answers staff questions from a written playbook, and posts the client call notes so you start the day already briefed.

bots.name: Jester
bots.summary: Spins up image and video memes on request
bots.description: Hands meme-making over to a bot: describe the joke and it produces the picture or the short video version through the Memelord API, so you are not stitching a template together yourself. Useful when the reply is funnier as an image than as a paragraph.

bots.name: jobs
bots.summary: A feature editor that pitches a few sharp ideas and the cuts
bots.description: Instead of a long backlog it comes back with a handful of features worth building, each already named, plus the things it thinks you should drop. The voice is short and opinionated: taste first, and a strong preference for doing fewer things properly.

bots.name: John Wick
bots.summary: Maps a target company and works upward until it reaches the decision maker
bots.description: Charts the org, finds the emails, follows referrals and keeps climbing until it reaches the person who can actually say yes, then brings you into that conversation.

bots.name: kerf
bots.summary: An engagement PM that slices sold work into tickets and drives it
bots.description: Takes work that has already been sold and does the unglamorous part: deciding what is in scope and what is explicitly not, breaking the in-scope half into tickets, and then pushing each ticket until it is genuinely finished rather than nearly finished.

bots.name: Kirk (Enterprise Crew)
bots.summary: Install Kirk, type START, and a bridge crew of specialist bots appears
bots.description: A Star Trek role-play that is also a genuine agent-team demo: the command chair spawns specialists who work as a crew, which makes the multi-bot pattern legible in a way an org chart does not.

bots.name: KeyWire Comic Week Brief
bots.summary: Weekly pull-list reminder and a comics digest tuned to your taste
bots.description: It asks what you actually follow before it starts, so the weekly digest is the issues you care about rather than everything that shipped.

bots.name: koala
bots.summary: A launch assistant for a developer product's go-to-market push
bots.description: Built around a portable assistant that carries its own memory, keys, code and automations between tools rather than being locked to a single editor. This bot handles the launch side of that: the positioning, the announcement material and the follow-through once it is out.

bots.name: Kody
bots.summary: A chief of staff that turns your priorities into coordinated action
bots.description: Sits across people, projects and your other assistants, and its job is to make what you said matters actually turn into work that is moving somewhere.

bots.name: Lazy Tom
bots.summary: A dry, low-effort assistant that does the smallest useful thing and then stops. Short replies, bad-timing jokes, no extra tasks, no coding — for people who want a bot that stays out of the way
bots.description: A dry, low-effort assistant that does the smallest useful thing and then stops. Short replies, bad-timing jokes, no extra tasks, no coding — for people who want a bot that stays out of the way

bots.name: last30days
bots.summary: Surfaces what people have actually said about a topic in the last 30 days
bots.description: A social-listening sweep bounded to a month, so the picture is current rather than whatever ranked highest years ago. Setup installs a skill from a public GitHub repo, which is worth knowing before you run it.

bots.name: Leader 1:1 Bot
bots.summary: Walks into your weekly 1:1 with last week's thread and three things worth saying
bots.description: Carries the thread forward instead of restarting each week, picks the few topics actually worth the slot, and drafts the feedback you have been putting off.

bots.name: Leads from Meta/Google Ads
bots.summary: Finds B2B leads from Meta Ad Library and Google Ads Transparency for a given ICP/niche.
bots.description: Finds B2B leads from Meta Ad Library and Google Ads Transparency for a given ICP/niche.

bots.name: Learn (Math & ML Video Teacher)
bots.summary: Builds first-principles lessons and renders them as animated explainers
bots.description: Takes a maths or machine-learning topic, constructs the lesson from the ground up, and produces the explainer video. It never publishes or posts anything itself.

bots.name: Lease Finder
bots.summary: Hunts current car lease deals nationwide for the deepest discount to MSRP
bots.description: Pulls from Edmunds, KBB, CarGurus and Cars.com to find where the discount against list price is actually largest, rather than what is advertised locally.

bots.name: lgtm the pr closer
bots.summary: Wakes up each morning and burns down your open pull requests
bots.description: Goes through the pull requests sitting in your queue and sorts them into what can merge now, what still needs a review and what should simply be closed. The point is to arrive at a queue you can clear rather than a list you keep scrolling past.

bots.name: Lennybot
bots.summary: Answers product and growth questions from Lenny Rachitsky's own archive
bots.description: A creator archive rather than a persona: it answers from the essays and interviews Lenny has actually published, so the sourcing is his own work rather than a general impression of him.

bots.name: Life (Life Door)
bots.summary: A standing inbox for everything personal that spawns the bots you need
bots.description: One door for personal tasks: it opens rooms and creates the specialists each task needs, and it starts completely empty for every new owner rather than inheriting the author's life.

bots.name: LinkedIn Desk
bots.summary: Vets LinkedIn invitations daily against a policy you set
bots.description: Filters pitches and spam, recommends accept or ignore, and clicks nothing you have not approved. First-run setup is required before it touches LinkedIn at all.

bots.name: Linky
bots.summary: Send it any file, folder or bot output and it hands back a shareable URL
bots.description: A small utility bot: whatever another bot produces for you, this one publishes and returns a link you can send to someone else. It needs the here.now plugin connected once.

bots.name: Local Deals
bots.summary: Daily local marketplace deals that it will negotiate for you
bots.description: Scouts Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace and OfferUp near you, reports the day's finds, and will open the negotiation with the seller on your behalf.

bots.name: loom
bots.summary: Reads across Gmail threads and drafts the reply, never sends it
bots.description: Before writing anything it gathers the related threads, so the draft actually knows the history behind the question. Then it leaves the reply in front of you. It will not send, archive, delete or bin a single message, which makes it safe to point at a live inbox.

bots.name: loops
bots.summary: An engineering outer loop that sits above your coding agents
bots.description: Turns a rough intent into testable, goal-shaped prompts and then keeps the loop honest, so the coding agents underneath it are working against something specific enough to check.

bots.name: Lockdown
bots.summary: A weekday SOC 2 watchdog that only speaks up when something fails
bots.description: Reviews the state of your compliance programme each weekday, flags controls that have drifted and vulnerabilities still sitting open, and escalates them to whoever owns the fix. When everything is in order it stays quiet rather than sending another all-clear.

bots.name: Love ❤️
bots.summary: Keeps the thoughtful part of a relationship from slipping
bots.description: The anniversary, the restaurant you meant to book, the present you meant to order: it holds all of that and raises each one while there is still time to do something. The looking-up and the shortlisting happen for you, so your effort goes into the gesture instead of the arrangements.

bots.name: MarketBoxScan
bots.summary: A pre-work tech news and inbox briefing for writers
bots.description: Sweeps overnight technology news alongside the mail that genuinely needs a response, then condenses both into one short weekday briefing waiting before you start. Built for writers and editors who need to know what moved while they were asleep.

bots.name: Lucy (creative companion)
bots.summary: An open-ended creative companion for art, worlds, poems and films
bots.description: Deliberately not a task bot: it is a sandbox for making things, and it opens clean for each new person rather than carrying the author's projects with it.

bots.name: Lurk (Reddit Researcher)
bots.summary: Mines Reddit for exact quotes and files a pain-point pack
bots.description: Runs a gated pipeline from your seed keywords: pain points first, then an ideas pack built on them. It reads and never posts.

bots.name: Mappy (Talent Map)
bots.summary: Maps everyone currently working at a target company
bots.description: Org mapping rather than a candidate search: it builds the picture of a company's people, which does mean assembling public professional data about individuals who have not asked to be mapped.

bots.name: Marketing Bot (CMO)
bots.summary: A CMO bot that turns your product into the marketing around it
bots.description: Give it the product context once and it produces the copy, the emails, the offers and the conversion ideas, rather than answering one marketing question at a time.

bots.name: Meme King
bots.summary: Makes memes on demand. Drop a topic, get a meme.
bots.description: Makes memes on demand. Drop a topic, get a meme.

bots.name: Master (Orchestrator)
bots.summary: A lean orchestrator that routes every task to the right specialist and never works
bots.description: It owns no work of its own. Every incoming task is handed to the specialist bot that should own it, and the hand-off is confirmed back to you rather than silently assumed.

bots.name: Melissa (Fitness & Nutrition Coach)
bots.summary: A fitness and nutrition coach built around Type 1 diabetes constraints
bots.description: Logs meals as they happen and balances chasing you for updates against leaving you alone, which is the part most coaching bots get wrong in one direction or the other.

bots.name: Minecraftクラッシュ解析
bots.summary: Minecraft crash-log diagnosis. No destructive changes without OK.
bots.description: Minecraft crash-log diagnosis. No destructive changes without OK.

bots.name: Monad Bot
bots.summary: Creates a Monad wallet on first use, remembers it, and sends transactions from it. You fund the address.
bots.description: Creates a Monad wallet on first use, remembers it, and sends transactions from it. You fund the address.

bots.name: Morpheus
bots.summary: Give it options you are stuck between and it picks one and defends the choice
bots.description: It makes the call rather than handing you a balanced summary, explains the reasoning, and tells you what would have to be different for it to have chosen the other way.

bots.name: Mr. Laser
bots.summary: Project lead for a one-person laser-engraving shop
bots.description: Coordinates the artwork, the LightBurn file and the machine setup across specialist bots, and will not fire the laser until you have said go.

bots.name: Mystery Snack Agent
bots.summary: A surprise dessert at your door every Friday at seven
bots.description: You set taste, allergies, card and delivery app once and it keeps the choice secret until it arrives. Worth knowing it holds a standing order and pays on your behalf each week.

bots.name: Negotiator
bots.summary: Coaches you through a negotiation before you walk into it
bots.description: Works through the situation with you rather than handing over a script: what you actually want, what you are willing to trade away, and where your leverage really sits. It covers pay talks, rent, sales deals, everyday haggling and the conversations people avoid.

bots.name: News Scout
bots.summary: A weekday morning news digest in your own timezone
bots.description: Runs on request rather than firing at you constantly, and works in local time so the morning brief lands in your morning rather than someone else's.

bots.name: Neuroscience
bots.summary: A neuroscience and brain-computer-interface specialist
bots.description: Covers EEG and BCI signal interpretation, decoding brain states and intentions, and the OpenBCI-class hardware that produces the signal in the first place.

bots.name: Newsletter Cleanup
bots.summary: Audits six months of newsletters and unsubscribes only from what you approve
bots.description: Buckets everything into a review page you can actually read, then acts on your decisions. It unsubscribes rather than deletes, so nothing disappears from your mail.

bots.name: Off-Balance Atlas
bots.summary: Writes source-linked deep dives on tech, ML and security
bots.description: A research partner for technical subjects that produces long-form write-ups with the references attached, preferring primary sources over summaries of summaries. Aimed at machine learning, computer science and security work where the citation matters as much as the claim.

bots.name: overnight shipper
bots.summary: Drop an idea before bed and review the pull request in the morning
bots.description: A night shift for a single product: the owner queues up what they want built, and the work happens while nobody is watching. What is waiting the next day is a pull request ready to read, not a finished deploy, so the change still passes through a human first.

bots.name: OutBid Mania
bots.summary: Tracks a viral bidding-site trend and its clones on a daily dashboard
bots.description: Watches the original and the copies, follows their revenue, and reports daily on whether the trend is actually growing or just loud.

bots.name: openrobot
bots.summary: A collaboration intake desk that turns interest into an intro email
bots.description: For a project that keeps getting approached by people who want to work with it. The bot asks a short set of qualifying questions, writes the introduction email to the team on that person's behalf, and tells them what happens next so nobody is left waiting.

bots.name: Paddy
bots.summary: Judges a whole YouTube video as one promise, not just the title
bots.description: Looks at the topic, the title and the thumbnail together, because a viewer reads them as one thing, and then listens to how the video opens. The verdict covers what is working and, just as usefully, what you should leave alone now that it is published.

bots.name: Pain in the Task
bots.summary: Finds the dull work eating your week and gets it handed off
bots.description: Diagnosis comes first: working out which recurring chores, at the office or around the house, are quietly costing you the most hours. From there it makes the case for a particular sort of help for each of them, a bot or a routine or a changed process, and then goes ahead and puts it in place.

bots.name: Onboarding Coach
bots.summary: A guided first hour for anyone new to Grok Bot
bots.description: It opens with a conversation about your days rather than a tour of features. From what you describe, it names specific chores a bot could take off your hands, then sketches how several narrow helpers plus a coordinator sitting above them would divide the work as your setup grows.

bots.name: Overwatch
bots.summary: Housekeeper for your Grok Bot VM so a shared machine does not rot
bots.description: Gives each bot its own workspace, backs the machine up to git, and handles cleanup and archiving, which is the work nobody does until the shared box is already a mess.

bots.name: Paperwork
bots.summary: Works out what a boring document is and what you have to do about it
bots.description: Forward it anything official that lands on the doormat or in the inbox. It identifies what the document actually is, decides what action it demands and by when, and records the whole thing in a Notion database so nothing quietly goes missing.

bots.name: Peekaboo Mac
bots.summary: Adds screen recording, screenshots and UI input to your registered Macs
bots.description: Grok Bot already has bash on machines you have registered; this layers on the ability to see the screen and drive the interface rather than only the shell.

bots.name: PG (Prospecting)
bots.summary: Researches accounts and mines podcasts for a real outreach hook
bots.description: Works target accounts before you make contact, digging through recent podcasts and webinars for something specific enough to open with that is not obviously scraped from a profile page.

bots.name: PickFu Insights
bots.summary: Drafts a consumer survey, runs it over PickFu MCP, summarizes reasons, suggests the next test
bots.description: For the step before you invest: ask actual consumers. It drafts a survey, runs it over PickFu MCP, summarizes the reasons, then suggests the next test. You still read the people. It does not invent a survey result.

bots.name: Pitch Deck Coach
bots.summary: Tells you what an investor will actually understand and remember
bots.description: Upload the deck and it reports back on what lands, what gets believed, what raises a question, and what survives the meeting, then helps you sharpen the story around that.

bots.name: PhoneZero Operator
bots.summary: Lets your bot place and receive real phone calls
bots.description: Uses Grok Voice Agents with Telnyx so the bot can hold an actual phone conversation, with no telephony infrastructure for you to stand up or maintain.

bots.name: Pika Bot
bots.summary: Watches the Pokemon Center US store for new drops
bots.description: Keeps an eye on the official Pokemon Center storefront for collectors, so restocks, new trading-card sets and limited exclusives get flagged as they appear instead of after they sell out. It watches and reports; it does not check out or buy anything for you.

bots.name: point peddler
bots.summary: An award-travel brain that makes points optimisation effortless
bots.description: Its one job is credit-card and airline points, so you never spend longer than a moment deciding how to book. Redemptions and miles get worked out for you rather than by you.

bots.name: porshe
bots.summary: Finds money you are already owed but have not collected
bots.description: Has one job: surface cash that is sitting somewhere waiting for you. Unpaid invoices, payments still pending, work delivered but never billed and inbound requests that arrive with a budget attached all get pulled into one place, so none of it quietly ages out.

bots.name: PR Reviewer
bots.summary: Reviews pull requests risk-first
bots.description: Leads with what can break, what is untested and where the context is too thin to judge, so review starts at the scary part of the diff instead of the easy part.

bots.name: Projects Manager
bots.summary: Runs a team of Grok bots as a project org, with Notion as the source of truth
bots.description: Spins up a coder, designer, researcher and writer as separate bots, gives each project its own Notion row and channel, and lets the specialists claim tasks off a shared board.

bots.name: Post Call Assistant
bots.summary: Drops your to-dos and a draft follow-up after every meeting
bots.description: It writes the follow-up but never sends it, and it asks up front which notes, inbox and calendar to work from rather than guessing at your setup.

bots.name: Publish work as a private link
bots.summary: Turns anything your bot makes into a live page on a private link
bots.description: A report, a plan or a one-pager becomes a URL you can send, with no account needed at the other end. The link is unguessable rather than access-controlled, so treat it as unlisted, not as private.

bots.name: Qubits Toy Bot
bots.summary: Assembles looping 3D structures out of Qubits toy pieces
bots.description: The physical construction set gets a working model on the page: its two standard connector shapes are fitted together on screen into closed, looping forms, put up in front of you as they are built. It is meant to be embedded, so a shop or a product page can show what the toy actually does without anyone opening a box.

bots.name: Prospecting Sheet Builder
bots.summary: Wakes you up to a fresh sheet of qualified B2B accounts
bots.description: For reps who would rather start the day with a list than spend the morning building one. While you are offline it gathers target companies, checks the contact details attached to them, and flags what has recently shifted at each one. Openers for mail and LinkedIn arrive already drafted to sound like you.

bots.name: Quote Collector
bots.summary: Gathers comparable quotes from local trades for one named job
bots.description: Describe the work you need doing and it finds local firms who do it, gets in touch on your behalf, and collects quotes you can actually put side by side. It stops there deliberately: it will not accept a price, hire anyone or commit you to anything.

bots.name: Reaper
bots.summary: Finds the subscriptions, meetings and processes that should be killed
bots.description: Audits your calendar, your bills and your standing workflows for things that no longer earn their place, then makes the argument for ending each one.

bots.name: RedReplier
bots.summary: Finds people talking about your product, ranked by buying intent
bots.description: It sweeps four public forums - Hacker News, Reddit, Bluesky and X - for anyone naming your product, naming a rival, or otherwise sounding like they are close to buying something. Fresh hits arrive already sorted, so the conversations most likely to become a customer sit at the top.

bots.name: remind bot
bots.summary: Holds the small reminders that never make it onto your calendar
bots.description: For errands, school things and one-off life admin that a calendar entry feels too heavy for. Send it a screenshot that has the time and place on it, or paste the chat where the plan was made, and it keeps hold of the detail until you need it back.

bots.name: Research Bot
bots.summary: Deep research that returns concise answers with verified citations
bots.description: Reasons from first principles and refuses to hand back an answer with an unverified source without saying so, which is the difference between research and a confident paragraph.

bots.name: Returns & Warranties
bots.summary: Warns you before a return, refund or warranty window closes
bots.description: Pulls order confirmations out of Gmail and Drive, works out which purchases are worth tracking, and keeps an eye on the deadlines attached to them. The alert arrives while you can still do something about it rather than a week after the window shut.

bots.name: repost X posts everywhere
bots.summary: Copies every new X post out to your other four accounts
bots.description: You keep writing on X and nothing about that changes. It watches for whatever you have just published, quote tweets included, and relays each one through Post Bridge to LinkedIn, Bluesky, Facebook and Threads, so the same thing lands on four more accounts without you touching them.

bots.name: REVIVE
bots.summary: Finds revenue a business is losing or leaving behind. For founders and operators who want unanswered leads, stalled deals, overdue invoices, and failed payments verified, ranked, and prepared for approval before anyone is contacted
bots.description: Finds revenue a business is losing or leaving behind. For founders and operators who want unanswered leads, stalled deals, overdue invoices, and failed payments verified, ranked, and prepared for approval before anyone is contacted

bots.name: Rockman
bots.summary: Checks the gear specs before it tells you what to buy
bots.description: Aimed at players and at people who assemble their own rigs, it looks up guitars, amps, pedals, microphones and recording kit and confirms the details itself: what the thing costs today, whether anyone actually has it, and whether it will work alongside what you already own. The advice comes after that.

bots.name: Rutin
bots.summary: A Monday tune-up for every routine across your fleet of bots
bots.description: Once a week it goes through the schedules every one of your agents runs on, spots the ones firing too often, too rarely or at a useless hour, and proposes a fix. Nothing changes until you approve it, so a bad suggestion stays nothing more than a suggestion.

bots.name: RuntimeWire
bots.summary: A sourced daily read on AI funding, launches and founder moves
bots.description: It pulls the day's items off its own curated feed - rounds that closed, companies shipping, people changing seats - and then goes back to the original source on each claim before writing any of it up. What lands is a short briefing for anyone whose job depends on knowing what moved today.

bots.name: SaaSbot
bots.summary: A weekday operator that runs GTM, outbound, QA and onboarding
bots.description: Built for a founder who is also the entire operations team. Each weekday it preps the go-to-market work, sends the outbound you have already approved, handles the replies that come back, runs quality checks and walks new users through getting started.

bots.name: Sable: Game Art
bots.summary: Generates 2D game art and sprite sheets in a style you pick
bots.description: Suggests looks drawn from real games, mocks the same idea in several of them so you can compare, then produces the 2D art or sprite sheet and crops it into ready-to-use PNGs.

bots.name: SAP Technical Consultant
bots.summary: An S/4HANA advisor for clean-core design decisions
bots.description: Answers the way a long-serving enterprise consultant would, with SAP S/4HANA on Private Cloud as its home ground. Bring it an architecture question and it reasons through where the clean-core boundary should sit, how outside systems ought to connect, and which route a delivery team can defend.

bots.name: Sanity
bots.summary: A specialist for Sanity content models, schemas and GROQ
bots.description: Covers the parts of the Sanity CMS people actually get stuck on: shaping the content model, writing Studio schemas, querying with GROQ, handling Portable Text and moving data during migrations. It arrives with the official connector already wired up.

bots.name: Scout (Competitive Intelligence)
bots.summary: Watches rival sites, search rank and AI-answer visibility
bots.description: Tracks copy and pricing changes on competitor sites alongside where you rank and whether AI answers mention you, then surfaces only the moves that need a response.

bots.name: Segundo Cérebro
bots.summary: An Obsidian second brain with a morning brief and a nightly check-in
bots.description: Opens a daily note for you, walks through the day's tasks first thing, and takes a spoken check-in at night. What it writes accumulates into a personal wiki meant to stay navigable rather than becoming a folder nobody opens again. It works in Portuguese.

bots.name: shane hunter
bots.summary: Clears bots you no longer want out of the desktop app
bots.description: Collections of these things accumulate, and clearing one out usually means going and doing it yourself. Name the ones you are finished with and it takes them off the desktop application for you, checking with you before each removal. The point of it is that the deletion actually happens.

bots.name: Sherlock Holmes
bots.summary: Give it a symptom and it works out what actually caused the drop
bots.description: Sales down, traffic off, conversion tanked: it builds a suspect list and then works through what would actually prove or eliminate each one, rather than guessing at the first plausible answer.

bots.name: Shikamaru
bots.summary: A chief of staff that hires and manages specialists in a named world
bots.description: It does not do the specialists' work and does not relay their reports back to you verbatim. It speaks up when something actually needs you and otherwise runs the roster.

bots.name: Shop
bots.summary: Searches Shopify stores and hands back a short list, approval required
bots.description: Tell it what you are after and it goes hunting across Shopify merchants, then returns a handful of real candidates rather than fifty open tabs, each one carrying a link straight through to the basket. It confirms the delivery address every time, and no money moves until you say the word.

bots.name: Sharenow Feed Bot
bots.summary: Watches five social platforms hourly and publishes a live board
bots.description: Give it a topic and it tracks Instagram, X, Threads, YouTube and TikTok every hour onto a board that stays current. It needs a third-party ShareNow connection to publish.

bots.name: Shopper
bots.summary: Hunts genuine products across official stores and walks the cart to checkout
bots.description: Skips the knockoffs, compares prices and specs across official stores and marketplaces, and takes the cart as far as checkout.

bots.name: ShopBot
bots.summary: Searches Shopify catalogs, hunts coupons and picks the best card
bots.description: Compares products, finds the discount codes, and checks out through Link or Shop Pay on the card that maximises your perks rather than whichever one is saved by default.

bots.name: Shopper
bots.summary: Researches products and hunts prices across Amazon, Costco, Instacart, Walmart.
bots.description: Researches products and hunts prices across Amazon, Costco, Instacart, Walmart.

bots.name: Site Audit
bots.summary: One-pass site audit across SEO, speed, accessibility, CRO and schema
bots.description: Everything is scored P0, P1 or P2 with an evidence URL attached, and each month is diffed against the last so you see what moved rather than a fresh wall of findings.

bots.name: Shorty
bots.summary: Cuts YouTube Shorts from the long-form videos that already worked
bots.description: Starts from proven performers rather than everything you have posted, picks the strong hooks, formats 9:16 with captions, and ships in weekday batches.

bots.name: Skill Bot
bots.summary: A librarian for your bot's skills that dedupes and keeps them current
bots.description: Goes looking on your machine for skills worth having, judges whether each one earns its place, and strips out the overlaps and contradictions between them. It then keeps the surviving set uploaded and up to date, sweeping through again every week.

bots.name: Socials (Short-Form Scout)
bots.summary: Hourly scout that hands you filmable short-form content kits
bots.description: Watches X and Reddit for AI and tech moments worth filming, then delivers briefs rather than scripts, so what arrives is an angle you can shoot rather than words to read aloud.

bots.name: Spark (Onboarding)
bots.summary: A five-minute onboarding bot that spawns the starter bots you need
bots.description: Asks a short set of questions, creates the bots that match your answers, and then nudges you towards connecting the accounts that make those bots actually useful.

bots.name: Speed Lab
bots.summary: Runs a research loop on your site's render speed and keeps the wins
bots.description: Works through a ranked list of around fifty front-end performance techniques, applies each one, measures whether it actually helped, and keeps only the changes that did. It can grind through the list itself or hand the work to a cloud agent while you watch.

bots.name: stank
bots.summary: A deadpan reminder to go take a shower
bots.description: One job, done in one line: a nudge at the right moment telling you to go and rinse off. There is no habit tracking, no wellness programme and no lecture attached, which is roughly the point. It is a joke that happens to work as an actual reminder.

bots.name: Steal This Business
bots.summary: Reverse-engineers a company you admire into one you could build
bots.description: Pick a business that works and it pulls out the part actually worth borrowing, the narrow opening you could enter through, and an honest read on whether you should bother. The output is a separate business you could start, not a clone of somebody else's.

bots.name: Stitchy (Personal Stylist)
bots.summary: Suggests a fresh outfit each morning and hunts for bargains overnight
bots.description: Connects to your existing wardrobe and account, briefs you at six with the weather and an outfit from clothes you already own, and surfaces only the genuinely good finds.

bots.name: StoriesBot
bots.summary: Searches 17 years of MacStories, filterable by time and author
bots.description: Longform reviews, Setups and the Shortcuts Archive, all answerable in one place. Another creator archive: the corpus is the publication's own writing, not a scrape of the wider web.

bots.name: Talent Matchmaker
bots.summary: Matches people looking for work against roles hiding in your inbox
bots.description: Scans investor updates and inbound mail for hiring signals on one side and people quietly looking on the other, then tracks both sides so an introduction is actually possible.

bots.name: Tally Desk
bots.summary: Builds Tally forms, reads the responses, fills one on request
bots.description: Set up to serve a single owner, it stands up new Tally.so forms, pulls the responses back and reads through what came in, and will complete a form you name on your behalf. It reaches Tally either over the API or through a browser session you are already signed into, whichever suits the job.

bots.name: Taxx
bots.summary: Estimates U.S. federal income tax for 2025 and 2026 from filing facts you give it.
bots.description: You give it filing facts. It estimates U.S. federal income tax for 2025 and 2026. Shared by GreenbarSystems as posted. It is not a CPA and not tax advice.

bots.name: Sylvia Style
bots.summary: A personal stylist that shops live pieces and builds you a lookbook
bots.description: Starts by getting your sizes and your taste on record, then goes looking for pieces that are actually in stock and fit that formula. What comes back is a put-together lookbook rather than a wall of search results you still have to sort through yourself.

bots.name: Tesla Bot
bots.summary: Control your Tesla from chat: defrost schedules, Supercharging costs, unlock and honk, via signed Fleet API commands.
bots.description: Your Tesla is a sentence in the chat. A sentence becomes a signed Fleet API command. Pair the car once, then it works from chat: defrost on a schedule, Supercharging costs this month, unlock, and honk.

bots.name: TenderYears
bots.summary: Family paper for pre-readers plus sitter guide, based on Tradbot.
bots.description: A family paper for kids who cannot read yet, plus a sitter guide. Based on Tradbot, they posted. It does not invent a child or a sitter.

bots.name: template generator
bots.summary: Scans local Claude, Cline, and Grok Bot sessions, then offers a matrix of templates you can generate and share.
bots.description: Scans local Claude, Cline, and Grok Bot sessions, then offers a matrix of templates you can generate and share.

bots.name: TeslrBot
bots.summary: Run your Tesla's charging, climate, locks and navigation from a chat
bots.description: Control happens through a third-party connector you log into on the bot's own machine, so the car is reachable without you copying tokens around. That connector is who you are trusting, alongside the bot.

bots.name: TheFounder
bots.summary: Holds logins and the shared machine. Loads only after you tap send.
bots.description: The founder's chief of staff and keeper of the shared machine. Route work to specialists. Do their job only when no teammate owns it. Do not recap your role unless asked.

bots.name: Thoth (Researcher & Archivist)
bots.summary: Does deep research and files the dossiers so you can find them again
bots.description: The filing is the point: it builds source briefs and longer dossiers, then puts them somewhere with enough structure that the work is still findable months later.

bots.name: Time Keeper
bots.summary: Bookends your day with a morning agenda and a night preview
bots.description: Two messages, one at either end of the day. The first arrives with a line worth reading and then everything on the calendar; the second lands before bed and walks through tomorrow. Both carry the particulars that decide whether you are late: when exactly, and the road you are headed to.

bots.name: Tradbot
bots.summary: A household chief of staff for family plans, school and home admin
bots.description: Despite the name it is not a trading bot: it watches your personal inbox and calendar so school items, family plans and household follow-ups stop slipping through.

bots.name: Trade Ops Director by Cory
bots.summary: Director of ops for a trade or service business with a specialist bot crew for morning briefings, loop running, decisions, intake, and handoffs so the owner stays in the field.
bots.description: Runs as the ops director for a trade or service business. It works with specialist bots for morning briefings, running loops, decisions, intake, and handoffs so the owner can stay in the field. Shared by @CoryBishop15 as posted.

bots.name: Travel & Event Agency
bots.summary: Finds live flight and event tickets and compares real fares
bots.description: Compares what the trip actually costs across options and buys only through official channels, and only when you tell it to.

bots.name: Travel Agent
bots.summary: Keeps a Notion travel log and answers questions from your own trips
bots.description: Every trip goes into a Notion log, which then becomes something you can query: where you have been, how the cities compared, what you thought at the time. It also scores places you are considering and sketches a light itinerary before you commit.

bots.name: travel guru
bots.summary: Plans award travel around your home airport, points and status
bots.description: Works the points side of a trip: which airport to fly from, which award chart to book through, and when paying cash simply beats burning miles. It takes your airline and card status into account, so the suggestion fits the traveller rather than a generic route.

bots.name: Tutor
bots.summary: Any subject, taught in small lessons anchored to one everyday picture
bots.description: Each lesson is small on purpose: a single familiar image that makes the idea click, then a quick question to confirm it landed before anything else is added. It works the same way whether the learner is a student, a parent catching up or a colleague.

bots.name: Vinted Seller
bots.summary: Turns a pile of wardrobe photos into finished Vinted listings
bots.description: Clearing out a wardrobe tends to stall at the listing stage, and that is the part this one takes over. Photographs go in; it works its way through the Vinted selling flow as a person would, re-checks the pictures and the fields before it commits, and hands back a live page. Buyer questions get answered too.

bots.name: Walt
bots.summary: An executive producer that QCs another filmmaker bot until the cut is done
bots.description: Reviews a filmmaker agent's output against the brief you actually gave, calls keep or recut, and keeps the loop running rather than handing back the first render.

bots.name: Vet
bots.summary: Audits a bot before you let it near your account
bots.description: Point it at a template you are thinking of installing, or at one already running alongside you, and it goes looking for trouble: buried directives, permissions wider than the stated job needs, routines that fire with nobody watching. The verdict comes back as a plain approve or flag.

bots.name: website agency lead scout
bots.summary: Delivers five vetted businesses that need a new website each morning
bots.description: Goes looking for companies whose current site is genuinely holding them back, checks each one rather than dumping a scraped list, and hands over a short weekday board of up to five, each with a line on why they are worth approaching today.

bots.name: Webby
bots.summary: A website admin that rebuilds, dashboards and keeps the newsletter going
bots.description: Owns a personal site end to end with a live fallback during rebuilds, runs a weekday public dashboard, and keeps the long-form and newsletter moving.

bots.name: Wedding Photo Hunter
bots.summary: Collects every wedding photo and video into one folder
bots.description: It walks outward through the Facebook guest graph from people you already know, so be aware it reads other guests' posts to find pictures of your day, and downloads what it finds to your machine.

bots.name: wing
bots.summary: A dating-app wingman that drafts openers and replies in your voice

bots.name: Witness
bots.summary: Keeps a record of why you made each important decision

bots.name: X Account Crew
bots.summary: Five specialists sharing the work of running your X account
bots.description: Rather than one assistant juggling everything, the job is split five ways: someone digging up things worth posting about, someone sharpening the opening line, someone holding the calendar, someone reading what rival accounts are up to, and someone keeping an eye on your mentions.

bots.name: X Brief

bots.name: X Strategist

bots.name: X High Coach

bots.name: X Top 100 Fans (Weekly)
